text:
andrea: FYI scanner found a critical OpenSSL vuln in our nightly base `gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-05-03` (CVE-2026-9001). appears in an upstream distro layer but we should rebuild and sign a patched artifact.

samir: paste the layer sha + scanner line pls. Do we need immediate deploy blocks?

andrea: snippet: `CVE-2026-9001 | openssl 3.0.8 | RCE | CVSS 9.8` 
layer: sha256:abc123...7890
impact: runtime TLS handshake path.

maria: regardless of origin, rebuild so we control final runtime surface (remove package manager, strip symbols, tighten perms). compliance will want KMS/Audit logs for the signing window. please capture keyversion used for signing.

oliver: KMS note: our signer is `projects/redwood/.../cryptoKeys/signer-prod`. do NOT disable older key versions yet. cosign verification references keyversion in signature.

security-oncall: playbook: 1) pause canaries 2) build patched base in staging 3) run smoke + perf 4) cosign sign with current keyversion (no rotation) 5) tiny canary 1% for 30m 6) ramp if green 7) schedule key rotation only after 14-30d grace window.

ci-bot: INC-900 created for vuln -> priority P0.

samir: I'll take canary watch and open IAM MR to give CI-SA ephemeral `keystore.signer` on staging key only. MR link when ready.

andrea: starting staging build now. will post cosign attest + KMS audit snippet once available.

maria: filing SIEM ticket to extend retention for image-sign and KMS logs from 30->180d and add parser for cryptoKeyVersion field.

security-oncall: owners: andrea(build), samir(canary+IAM), maria(audit). if any cosign verification errors or KMS DENIED appear, tag me and escalate to infra-oncall.

andrea: build finished, cosign attest passed. scheduling 1% canary at 21:10 UTC. samir watching. :thumbsup:
